Indikator 6 tracks the proportion of prevalent patients with [[atrieflimren]] who experience an admission for [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]]. The established national standard for this indicator is a maximum threshold of 0.6% (≤ 0.6%) [^src1] [^src2].

For the 2022–2023 period, the national average in Denmark was 0.5%, successfully meeting the target [^src1]. At the regional level, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] (0.5%), [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] (0.5%), [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] (0.4%), and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] (0.5%) all met the standard [^src1]. In contrast, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] missed the target, recording a rate of 0.7% [^src1].

A closer look at the municipal level during the 2022–2023 period reveals significant local variation. Within the Capital Region, the highest rates (trailers) were recorded in [[alleroed|Allerød]] and [[frederiksvaerk-hundested|Frederiksværk-Hundested]] (both at 1.3%), followed by [[dragoer|Dragør]] (1.2%) [^src1]. Conversely, [[hoeje-taastrup|Høje-Taastrup]] and [[ishoej|Ishøj]] were the leaders, reporting 0.0% [^src1]. In Region Sjælland and Region Syddanmark, [[vallensbaek|Vallensbæk]] recorded the highest rate at 1.5%, with [[langeland|Langeland]] (1.1%) and [[billund|Billund]] (1.0%) also exceeding the threshold [^src2]. The lowest rates in these regions were seen in [[solrod]] and [[fanoe]] (both 0.0%), as well as [[soenderborg|Sønderborg]] (0.1%) [^src2].

Trends into the 2023–2024 period show notable improvements in regional compliance. The national average remained stable at 0.5% [^src3]. Crucially, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] reduced its rate from 0.7% to 0.6%, thereby meeting the standard in the latest period [^src3]. All five Danish regions successfully met the target in 2023–2024, with rates ranging between 0.5% and 0.6% [^src3]. However, at the health cluster level, outliers emerged: Sundhedsklynge Fyn and Klynge MIDT both recorded rates of 0.7%, failing to meet the ≤ 0.6% threshold [^src3].

Comprehensive methodological frameworks, broader clinical contexts, and additional indicator analyses supporting these findings are detailed throughout the 2023 and 2024 annual reports [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19] [^src20] [^src21] [^src22] [^src23] [^src24] [^src25] [^src26].
